Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Recording: Fireflies AI auto-record
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Dmitri Novak (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Solstice Head of Security), Maya Ortiz (VP Compliance), Ravi Patel (Lead DevOps), Samira Nadeem (Legal)

Summary: quick posture review for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope, discuss trust center access, evidence collection and controls mapping. Customer wants clarity on KMS options (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention and forwarding, RBAC & SSO provisioning, and data residency for EU workloads.

Topics: 1) reports & attestations (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001) 2) Trust Center access model 3) Controls mapping & evidence collection 4) KMS/encryption options and key rotation 5) Audit logging, retention, SIEM integration 6) RBAC, SSO (SAML/SCIM) and least privilege

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: okay, thanks everyone for joining, we wanted to keep this to about an hour, quick posture review and then next steps on controls mapping.
00:12 Alex Chen: yep thanks, we did a quick prep, Maya and I are looking to confirm the scope for SOC2 and ISO, primarily concerned about data residency and key management.
00:20 Priya: great, I'll start with the artifacts we have — SOC 2 Type II report for the period april-march, ISO 27001 certificate summary, and a trust center link where we host the control narratives and subprocessor list. I'll share links after the call.
00:35 Maya: is the trust center read-only? we need to give our audit team access to download evidence.
00:42 Jordan: yes, we can provide read-only access to the trust center and separate S3 links for compiled evidence. There are some items that are redacted in the public summary but the attestation PDF is available.
00:53 Ravi: quick Q on KMS — does Redwood support bringing our KMS (HSM) or only Redwood-managed keys? we need to keep keys under our control for certain PHI workflows.
01:05 Priya: we support a couple of models: Redwood-managed keys for hosted API, or customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / Cloud HSM for Dedicated or Private deployments. For private VPC we can integrate with your KMS and key rotation policies, but there's a small on-boarding checklist for crypto ops and IAM roles.
01:20 Alex Chen: timeline for that integration? we don't want a multi-month delay.
01:26 Dmitri: typical integration for KMS on Dedicated is 2-3 weeks for the initial PoC (key provisioning, IAM roles, test rotation), then a production cutover after acceptance. For Private on-prem it's longer because of network & audit requirements.
01:41 Maya: control mapping — we have our internal control IDs and we need to map to SOC 2 CC and ISO Annex A controls. do you provide a mapping template?
01:50 Priya: yes we have a spreadsheet template that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A clauses; we'll pre-fill common mappings for hosting, encryption, access control, change management.
02:02 Samira: legal will want confirmation on subprocessor list and data residency guarantees— specifically eu residency for certain datasets.
02:11 Jordan: subprocessor list is in the trust center. For data residency, we support region pinning on Dedicated and Private; hosted API offers region routing but not strict residency guarantees unless on a dedicated contract.
02:25 Ravi: on audit logs — what fields are captured and how long retained by default? we need user-id, request-id, model-id, prompt hash (redacted?), response size, latency and k-v cache ops for accountability.
02:40 Priya: default retention is 90 days for hosted logs, longer retention options available as an add-on for 1 year or custom retention on Dedicated. Logs include request metadata, anonymized prompts by default unless configured for e2e traceability; we can also forward syslog/CloudWatch/Datadog with structured fields.
02:57 Alex Chen: anonymized prompts are tricky — for regulated data we need full prompt retention for a short period and strict ACLs. How do we support that?
03:07 Priya: we can enable controlled retention for a customer under contract; that would require explicit config, SSO provisioning, and audit policies. If prompts are highly sensitive, customers often use Private deployment or token-level redaction rules.
03:22 Maya: SSO and provisioning — we use Okta, want SCIM for group provisioning and SAML for SSO; role-based access with least privilege.
03:33 Dmitri: Okta is our most common integration. We do SAML SSO + SCIM for groups and role sync. RBAC supports custom roles and resource scoping per-tenant. We'll provide sample SCIM mappings and recommended role templates.
03:49 Ravi: how immutable are audit logs — can they be tampered with? we need write-once storage or signed logs.
03:57 Priya: logs are shipped to append-only storage; for compliance we support log forwarding to your SIEM and can provide signed hash chains for attestation. For Dedicated we can enable WORM storage or export to your cloud bucket with object lock.
04:11 Alex Chen: incident response & breach notification SLAs?
04:18 Jordan: we have a documented IR plan with 72-hour notification for confirmed security incidents; enterprise customers can negotiate shorter timelines in the SLA. Incident reports are in the trust center and we can arrange an IR tabletop if needed.
04:31 Maya: on control evidence — will Redwood accept our control requests (like screenshots, config exports) or do we request them from you?
04:40 Priya: we provide evidence where possible (config exports, logs, runbooks) and we can also accept artifacts from customers for joint controls. The control mapping will indicate owner R (Redwood), C (Customer) or joint.
04:53 Samira: privacy questions — is there any hashing of PII at ingestion?
04:59 Dmitri: we offer option to do prefix hashing or token redaction on input, but it requires configuration. For the highest assurance we recommend isolated workloads in Private mode.
05:12 Ravi: network controls — what about egress filtering and VPC peering?
05:18 Priya: Private and Dedicated support VPC peering, IP allowlists, private endpoints; egress rules can be constrained. Hosted API is public but supports VPC-like peering in Dedicated.
05:30 Alex Chen: would you be able to map Redwood controls to our control IDs and return a gap analysis?
05:36 Jordan: yes, that's the standard engagement: we fill in the mapping for common controls and flag gaps; then we propose mitigation steps or required customer evidence.
05:46 Maya: on ISO 27001 certificate — do you have scope boundaries documented?
05:52 Priya: yes, ISO scope is services: inference platform, control plane, and managed hosting. The certificate summary lists excluded services like experimental research clusters. We'll share the scope doc.
06:05 Ravi: what's the process for evidence collection during our audit? will you upload evidence to a shared portal?
06:12 Jordan: we can provide read-only access to the trust center and S3 bundles; for on-prem audits we can also set up an ephemeral vault with time-bound access for auditors.
06:24 Alex Chen: great. For encryption, do you support key rotation windows and customer rotation schedules?
06:30 Dmitri: yes, rotation windows are configurable. If you bring your own KMS, rotation is per your policy; Redwood-managed keys rotate on a standard 90-day cadence but we can adjust for enterprise contracts.
06:43 Maya: any backlog items on continuous monitoring or quality of logs?
06:48 Priya: Redwood Optimize includes anomaly detection for latency and model drift, and we can expose evals and alerting to your SSO-enabled dashboards.
06:58 Samira: legal wants us to confirm the subprocessor notification cadence and termination assistance.
07:05 Jordan: we notify customers of subprocessor changes via the trust center and contract clauses; termination assistance is included in enterprise agreements.
07:14 Alex Chen: okay, sounds good. next steps?
07:18 Jordan: I'll share SOC2, ISO docs and trust center link (action). Priya will send the control mapping template and pre-filled mappings. Dmitri will prepare the KMS integration preview. Schedule the KMS deep dive with Ravi.
07:32 Maya: timeline — we'd like initial mapping back in a week so our audit team can review.
07:37 Jordan: we'll aim for the 9/22 delivery on the mappings.
07:42 Alex Chen: thanks everyone.
07:45 (end recording)
